findings.item: ~/.claude/rules/common/ exists but is EMPTY — 0 of 20 repo files materialized (windows-shell.md, static-analyzer.md, owner-ops-authorization.md, ci-hygiene.md, single-signal-verification.md, fan-out-contract.md, harness-vcs-hygiene.md, ...)

(dir entry present, created/last-modified 2026-09-03 17:06); (3) `find ... -mindepth 1 | wc -l` = 0. Repo side intact: rules/common holds 20 files (ls count 20; windows-shell.md 18586B, mtime 2026-08-10). Settling experiment run: `pwsh scripts/sync-rules.ps1 -WhatIf` (dry-run, no writes) today reports 'would sync 20 rule file(s) ... -> C:\Users\Prekzursil\.claude\rules\common', proving the bridge works and the dest simply never received the copy. findings.recommendation: Owner-approved write (outside this read-only lane): run `pwsh -File scripts/sync-rules.ps1` from the repo — non-destructive by design (copy-only, no prune), WhatIf-verified to land exactly the 20 managed files. Then add a rules/common guard (file-count >= 20 or per-file existence) to `agents doctor` / audit gates so a silent re-empty cannot recur.

findings.item: ADJACENT (outside lane's primary pair): ~/.codex/rules is a half-flattened, stale merge of the repo corpus
findings.evidence: 78 files at ~/.codex/rules: top level holds ONLY dart/ (5) + web/ (7) + default.rules; another 64 files sit under a NESTED rules/ subdir (~/.codex/rules/rules/...). Prefix-stripped hash compare of the nested tree vs repo: 65 path-matches, 46 identical, 19 REAL drift (all 9 nested common/* + README + golang/coding-style + java/testing + ...), and 23 repo files absent entirely (incl. windows-shell.md, static-analyzer.md, owner-ops-authorization.md, ci-hygiene.md). findings.recommendation: Route to whichever lane owns Codex config: flatten to one level and re-run a codex-targeted rules sync; treat the nested rules/rules/ artifact like the known 'platform layout checked into live folder' hazard class.

findings.item: CRLF phantom drift dominates the shared rules surface; zero real content drift in shared files
findings.evidence: repo rules/ -> ~/.claude/rules: 68 shared, 16 byte-identical, 52 differ ONLY by CRLF/LF (LF-normalized hashes equal), 0 real drift. Guides: 2 shared, both CRLF-only. Matches the estate memory note 'most drift is CRLF phantoms' — do not re-flag these as content drift in future audits.
findings.recommendation: Optional: normalize line endings at sync time so size-based drift checks stop tripping on phantoms.

summary: G-96 pointer chain: HEALTHY (resolves end-to-end; breakage is downstream, not in the chain). Headline defect: ~/.claude/rules/common/ is an EMPTY directory — 0 of the 20 repo rule files ever landed — so the §11 windows-shell hard-rules pointer (AGENTS-RUNTIME.md:171), the §0 owner-ops policy pointer (:18), and the static-analyzer pointer (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:21) all dangle on every live Claude session, and the live rules README contradicts the tree it sits in. Root cause is a sync gap, not content loss: the mandated sync_shared_state.ps1 has zero rules/guides handling, the designed bridge scripts/sync-rules.ps1 works (WhatIf dry-run verified: would copy 20 files, non-destructive) but has never successfully populated the dest since at least 2026-09-03, and no guides bridge exists at all. Shared per-language rules are content-clean (0 real drift; 52/68 CRLF-only). Guides trees are intentionally-forked-ish but undocumented (2 repo-only guides never materialized, unreferenced). Adjacent: ~/.codex/rules is a half-flattened stale merge (nested rules/rules/, 19+8 real-drift files, 23 repo files missing). One-command owner fix for the headline: run sync-rules.ps1 for real; then gate common/ file-count in agents doctor.
